summary: The game scaffold ships four import-and-adapt helper modules compiled by default; this product adopted two (Collision, Visibility) and never referenced the other two (Grids.fs, LineDrawing.fs), which compiled 282 unreachable lines into every build for the product's whole life with nothing reporting it.
evidence: file:src/Rogue3/Rogue3.fsproj; command:grep -rn 'Grids\.|LineDrawing|Los\.' src tests --include=*.fs returns no hit outside the two files themselves; issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#19; deleting both kept dotnet test at 199/199 passed
cost: none for this removal (build and 199-test suite green first try); the unbounded cost is the dead compile weight carried since scaffold time
owner: FS-GG scaffold provider (game/sample-pack template helper set + generated Product.fsproj compile items)

summary: The scaffold map's delete instruction for the Exists-guarded helpers says deleting the file keeps the build green and 'you never touch the durable Product.fsproj', but following it verbatim leaves an orphan compile item and its four-line comment block pointing at a file that no longer exists, and leaves the map itself still listing the deleted file as shipped.
evidence: file:docs/scaffold-map.md; file:src/Rogue3/Rogue3.fsproj; the removed items were Compile Include="Grids.fs" Condition="Exists('Grids.fs')" and the LineDrawing.fs equivalent, each preceded by a Feature-numbered comment block
cost: none; one extra edit to Rogue3.fsproj and one to docs/scaffold-map.md beyond deleting the two source files
owner: FS-GG scaffold provider (docs/scaffold-map.md delete guidance for Exists-guarded helper source)

summary: Running the repo's mandated full gate inside a git worktree silently rewrites three TRACKED evidence artifacts into a falsely degraded state, because the gate senses readiness outputs that .gitignore keeps out of any fresh worktree: readiness files present dropped from 67 to 58 and nine evidence nodes vanished from the graph, none of which the change touched.
evidence: command:./fake.sh build -t Verify; file:.gitignore line 8 pattern readiness/*/*; file:readiness/evidence-graph.md changed '- readiness files present: 67' to '- readiness files present: 58'; also rewrote readiness/m7-ui-performance.json and readiness/performance-evidence.json; command:git check-ignore -v readiness/012-m11-playability-visual-legibility/verify.json confirms the sensed-but-absent files are gitignored
cost: none here (caught by diffing the gate's own output before staging); a worker who ran the mandated gate and staged with git add -A would have landed falsified evidence artifacts in the PR
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 (build.fsx evidence-graph/performance-evidence emitters vs .gitignore readiness/*/*), plus the worktree-per-worker orchestration guidance

summary: The independent fresh-context critic caught a false claim that had already been committed into the product tree: the draft, the Rogue3.fsproj comment and docs/scaffold-map.md all asserted the fs-gg-grids and fs-gg-line-drawing skills carry the deleted module source, when each skill holds only ~25 and ~14 lines of call-site examples against 176- and 106-line modules, so git history is the only route back. It also refuted the issue's own premise data, finding a third equally dead helper.
evidence: file:.agents/skills/fs-gg-grids/SKILL.md; file:.agents/skills/fs-gg-line-drawing/SKILL.md; command:git grep -n Visibility 1f19809 -- src tests shows only doc comments outside Visibility.fs; issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#28; corrected in commit 0aab1ff
cost: one amended commit and one extra issue; the counterfactual cost is a merged instruction telling a future milestone to re-add a module from a skill that does not contain it
owner: fs-gg-feedback-report skill (the independent-critic step) — evidence that the critic pass earns its cost when the author has already committed the error
